questions.question: In UK public spending by purpose, which area is the largest?

options.B: Social protection, including pensions and benefits

questions.why: Social protection is the largest function of UK public spending, with health usually second.

questions.question: Spending in pounds rose every year, yet spending as a share of GDP fell. How is this possible?

options.A: The economy grew faster than spending

questions.why: A share of GDP falls if the economy grows faster than spending, even when cash spending rises.

questions.question: Which best describes the national debt?

options.A: Money the government borrows in a single year
options.B: The total owed from past borrowing that has not yet been repaid
options.C: All tax collected in a year

questions.why: Borrowing in a year adds to the accumulated stock of debt.

questions.question: Which of these is counted as part of government spending?

options.C: Council tax bills not yet paid

questions.why: Debt interest is spending; tax receipts and borrowing are ways of funding it.

questions.question: Which three taxes raise the most money for UK central government?

options.A: Income tax, National Insurance and VAT
options.B: Fuel duty, stamp duty and alcohol duty
options.C: Corporation tax, tobacco duty and air passenger duty
options.D: Council tax, inheritance tax and VAT

questions.why: Income tax, National Insurance contributions and VAT are the three largest receipts.

questions.question: Is government borrowing a type of tax revenue?

options.A: Yes, it is the largest tax
options.C: No, it is money raised by issuing debt that must be repaid
options.D: No, it is a type of National Insurance

questions.why: Borrowing funds a gap between spending and receipts; it is not a tax.

questions.question: Who legally pays corporation tax?
questions.why: Corporation tax is charged on company profits.

questions.question: A tax series has a break in 2010 because the definition changed. How should a chart treat 2005 and 2015?

options.A: Show the break and not compare the two sides directly as if the same measure
options.B: Join the line smoothly as one measure
options.D: Guess an adjustment to the 2005 figure

questions.why: A break means the before and after figures are measured differently.

questions.question: Higher earners pay a large share of all income tax. What does this show on its own?

options.A: They pay the highest tax rate on every pound
options.B: Where the revenue comes from, not the rate anyone pays
options.D: That low earners pay no tax

questions.why: A share of revenue says who supplies the money, not the personal tax rate.

questions.question: If your pay rises just above the higher-rate threshold, how is the higher rate applied?

options.C: To your income above the threshold only
options.D: To your income below the threshold only

questions.why: Income tax rates apply to slices of income (bands).

questions.question: Council tax bills in England depend mainly on which feature of the home?
questions.why: Council tax is set by valuation band and the local authority's rate.

questions.question: Which statement about who pays tax can be true at the same time?

options.A: Richer households pay more pounds, poorer ones may pay a larger share on indirect tax
options.B: Everyone pays the same rate on all taxes

questions.why: Cash amounts and shares of income can point in different directions.

questions.question: Across the UK, indirect taxes such as VAT take a larger share of income from which group?

options.C: They take the same share from all

questions.why: Official analysis shows indirect taxes are regressive as a share of disposable income.

questions.question: An official table gives the average share of household income paid in tax. What does that average mean?

options.A: Every household pays exactly that share
options.B: Income tax is charged at that rate
options.C: It is a group average, not any one household's rate
options.D: It is the share of all tax that households raise

questions.why: A household average is neither a personal rate nor a share of total revenue.

questions.question: A website shows a 'typical family' paying £X in tax using assumed pay and spending. What is this?

options.A: An illustration built on assumptions, not a measured figure

questions.why: Illustrative households come from chosen assumptions rather than measured data.

questions.question: Direct taxes, such as income tax, take what share of gross income as household income rises?
questions.why: Direct taxes as a share of gross income are higher for richer households on average.

questions.question: Why can the number of jobs be higher than the number of people in work?

options.A: Some people hold more than one job
options.B: Jobs are counted before they begin

questions.why: A person with two jobs appears twice in a count of jobs.

questions.question: The employment rate is the share of which group who are in paid work?

options.B: People aged 16 to 64 or other stated age group

questions.why: Employment rate is employment divided by the population of the stated age group.

questions.question: Pay rose 3% in cash terms while prices rose 6%. What happened to pay after allowing for inflation?
questions.why: Prices rose faster than pay, so real pay fell.

questions.question: In England, which housing tenure has the most households?
questions.why: Owner occupation is England's largest tenure.

questions.question: Which country do UK residents visit most often on overseas holidays?
questions.why: Spain has long been the most common destination for UK residents' trips abroad.

questions.question: An average class size of 27 is quoted. What must you check before comparing it with another figure?
questions.why: Class size differs by nation and by primary or secondary phase, and definitions vary.

questions.question: Average class sizes fell over ten years. What can the figures alone tell you?

options.D: That class sizes changed, but not why

questions.why: Data show change over time; cause needs separate evidence.

questions.question: A holiday chart has no data for 2020 because the survey was not run. How should it be drawn?

options.A: Show a gap and say so
options.C: Join 2019 to 2021 with a straight line

questions.why: Missing years should be shown as missing, not filled in.
